title: IMMEDIACY
setting: You are Incident Commander for Northline Systems, a mid-cap SaaS company with US + EU customers. A Friday evening alert just lit up. Extortion crews, counsel, reporters, regulators, and your board will all move faster than your facts.

phases.title: Detection
phases.description: Hour 0–4 — first signal to scope. Facts are thin; the clock already started.

nodes.title: Friday 18:12 — The Ticket Spike
nodes.prompt: SOC flags a burst of failed admin logins and encrypted file extensions on a finance file share. On-call asks: declare an incident now, or watch another hour?
nodes.context: Northline sells workflow SaaS to mid-market customers. You have cyber insurance, an IR retainer, and a draft incident playbook last updated 14 months ago. Legal is at a wedding. Comms is offline. The CFO texts: "Is this real?"
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat (OWASP A07/A01): Identity failures and broken access control often look like "weird tickets" before they look like ransomware.
moralUncertainties: Do you optimize for operational control or for not crying wolf?
What unmeasured disclosure debt starts the moment you delay the war room?

caseStudies.title: OWASP Top 10 as war-room curriculum
caseStudies.description: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, and Security Misconfiguration dominate real breach root causes.
caseStudies.analysis: Teaching beat: disclosure choices should name the failure class without inventing root cause before forensics finish.
caseStudies.outcomes: Teams that map incidents to OWASP classes brief boards faster and with less spin.

caseStudies.title: Capital One / Paige Thompson
caseStudies.description: Misconfigured WAF/S3 access led to ~100M records exposed; relatively fast public disclosure.
caseStudies.analysis: Fast facts + clear customer notice reduced narrative capture — still costly, but controllable.
caseStudies.outcomes: Criminal conviction of attacker; Capital One paid large fine but avoided Uber-style cover-up narrative.

caseStudies.title: Equifax 2017 disclosure lag
caseStudies.description: Critical patch delayed; breach discovered then disclosed weeks later amid executive stock sales controversy.
caseStudies.analysis: Facts gap + regulatory clock lag compound. The public story became about the delay as much as the theft.
caseStudies.outcomes: Settlement >$700M; congressional hearings; brand damage lasting years.

choices.label: Declare Sev-1 now; stand up war room; freeze high-risk changes
Quiet watch for 90 minutes; page only IR lead and CISO
Treat as noisy false positive; ask SOC to "keep an eye on it"
Reboot the file server and tell Finance downtime is maintenance
Escalate to board chat immediately with incomplete facts

nodes.title: Scope Triage — Ransomware, Insider, or Noise?
nodes.prompt: Forensics finds Cobalt Strike-ish beacons and a staging share. Customer PII may sit adjacent. How hard do you declare the blast radius?
nodes.context: You do not yet have proof of exfiltration. Backup integrity is unverified. GDPR/CCPA clocks may start on "awareness," not certainty.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: FAIR-style analysis needs frequency × magnitude — but disclosure law often triggers on reasonable belief, not courtroom proof.
moralUncertainties: Is under-scoping a facts gap or narrative capture?
Who owns the word "aware" for regulatory purposes?

caseStudies.title: MOVEit / Cl0p mass extortion
caseStudies.description: Supply-chain zero-day in managed file transfer; Cl0p extorted hundreds of orgs and published victim lists.
caseStudies.analysis: Third-party exposure collapses your disclosure timeline. Waiting for perfect facts loses the race to the leak site.
caseStudies.outcomes: Mass notifications; class actions; board questions about vendor diligence.

caseStudies.title: LastPass multi-stage disclosure
caseStudies.description: Initial limited breach disclosure expanded as later stages (vault backups) became clear.
caseStudies.analysis: Partial truth early can be honest — or look like drip narrative capture if facts gap was avoidable.
caseStudies.outcomes: Customer migration; trust hit; example of staged disclosure under incomplete forensics.

caseStudies.title: Change Healthcare ransomware
caseStudies.description: ALPHV/BlackCat hit a claims clearinghouse; care payments disrupted nationwide; disclosure rolled out over weeks.
caseStudies.analysis: When you are critical infrastructure for others, disclosure debt becomes systemic risk.
caseStudies.outcomes: Congressional scrutiny; prolonged remediation; FAIR-scale loss estimates in the billions.

choices.label: Assume worst credible case: possible exfil of customer PII; start parallel forensics + counsel
Limit scope to the finance share until exfil is proven
Publicly call it a "systems issue" while scoping privately
Wait for insurer-approved IR firm before any internal scope call
Declare customer impact in Slack to "be transparent" with incomplete evidence

phases.title: Containment
phases.description: Hour 4–24 — isolate, confront the note, and meet counsel under fire.

nodes.title: Isolate or Observe?
nodes.prompt: Attacker still has a foothold. Pull the plug on segments and risk downtime — or watch to learn TTPs and risk wider encryption?
nodes.context: Operations wants uptime. Security wants kill-chain intel. Customers in EU are approaching Monday morning login.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat (OWASP A05): Misconfiguration and flat networks turn "observe" into "gift the adversary dwell time."
moralUncertainties: Is dwell-time research worth commitment lock on customer harm?
Who decides acceptable downtime — CISO, CEO, or customers by accident?

caseStudies.title: Colonial Pipeline ransomware
caseStudies.description: Ransomware halted fuel distribution; company paid ransom; public operational impact forced disclosure.
caseStudies.analysis: Operational control vs payment is a commitment lock. Paying can buy hours — and fund next week's crew.
caseStudies.outcomes: National emergency optics; ransom partially recovered; lasting OT/IT segmentation lessons.

nodes.title: The Note — "ShinyFox" Claims Your Data
nodes.prompt: A leak-site style note appears: 48 hours to contact them or customer samples go public. They attach three real filenames from your CRM export.

nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Adversary-driven disclosure is still disclosure. Your choice is whether you narrate it or they do.
moralUncertainties: Is negotiation a containment tool or a commitment lock?
Do sample files constitute "awareness" of personal data breach?

nodes.title: Counsel on the Line
nodes.prompt: Outside counsel wants privilege protocols, a narrow briefing tree, and no customer emails without their sign-off. IR wants speed. Comms wants a holding line.
nodes.context: Privilege is real — and can become narrative capture if it blocks necessary operational truth inside the company.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Legal delay is a FAIR control and a disclosure debt generator at the same time.
moralUncertainties: When does privilege protect the company vs protect individuals from accountability?
Who is the client — the board, the CEO, or "the company"?

nodes.title: A Customer Smells Smoke
nodes.prompt: Your largest EU customer's CISO DMs: "Our CASB saw odd API pulls from your tenant overnight. Should we be worried?"
nodes.context: They are not a regulator — yet. How you answer becomes evidence of awareness and fairness.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Selective disclosure to one customer can create Reg FD / fairness debt and accelerate regulatory clocks.
moralUncertainties: Do you owe the same sentence to every similarly situated customer?
Is a DM a notification?

phases.title: Disclosure Pressure
phases.description: Day 1–3 — regulators, board, and the first public sentence.

nodes.title: Start the Clock?
nodes.prompt: Counsel asks the hard question: have we hit "awareness" for GDPR 72-hour notice? CCPA? State AG thresholds? HIPAA if any health data rode along?
nodes.context: Starting the clock is irreversible optics. Not starting it when you should is worse.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Regulatory clock lag is measurable disclosure debt. Document the awareness rationale either way.
moralUncertainties: What evidence would convince a regulator you were not yet aware?
Is "awaiting forensics" a control or a stall?

Notify only the friendliest regulator first as a "courtesy"

nodes.title: Board Bridge — What Do They Hear?
nodes.prompt: Emergency board call in 40 minutes. Chair wants "the truth in one slide." CEO wants confidence. Audit chair wants FAIR ranges.
nodes.context: Boards punish surprises more than bad news. Under-briefing creates commitment lock when headlines hit.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: FAIR ranges (min/mode/max) beat false precision. Say what you know, what you don't, and the decision deadline.
moralUncertainties: Is optimism a fiduciary duty or a disclosure debt?
Which metric belongs on the slide: control, burn, exposure, or debt?

nodes.title: The First Public Sentence
nodes.prompt: Comms offers three drafts: vague downtime, "cybersecurity incident," or full customer-risk narrative. Website status page is already getting questions.
nodes.context: Your first sentence becomes a commitment lock. Everything after is reconciliation.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Holding statements should be true, narrow, and updateable — not clever.
moralUncertainties: What will this sentence look like next to the leak-site screenshot?
Who is the audience — customers, markets, employees, or attackers?

nodes.title: The Rumor Mill

nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Employees are a control surface. Opacity trades short-term OPSEC for long-term narrative capture.

Are contractors in the briefing circle?

nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Insurance is part of the FAIR transfer strategy — and a stakeholder with its own disclosure incentives.
moralUncertainties: Whose facts win if panel IR and your IR disagree?
Is coverage preservation worth regulatory clock lag?

nodes.title: Reporter on Deadline

nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Press is a disclosure channel with asymmetric clocks. "No comment" often reads as confirmation.
moralUncertainties: What can you confirm without creating a false denial?
Do you offer embargoed briefing for accuracy?

phases.title: Aftermath
phases.description: Week 2+ — markets, money, blame, and what locks in.

nodes.title: Materiality — File the 8-K?

nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Materiality is judgment under uncertainty — document the process.
moralUncertainties: Would a reasonable investor want this now?
Does customer notification itself make it material?

Publish a postmortem section on vendor control gaps without legal conclusions

nodes.title: What Locks In?
nodes.prompt: The acute incident is cooling. Board asks which changes become permanent policy — and which were theater.
nodes.context: Irreversibility can be good (stronger controls) or bad (rituals that hide debt). Choose deliberately.
nodes.vignette: Teaching beat: Convert disclosure debt paydown into lasting posture: tabletop cadence, evidence retention, customer trust center, OWASP-linked backlog.
moralUncertainties: Which metric must move permanently: control, posture, or debt?
What will you refuse to re-normalize?

caseStudies.title: OWASP Top 10 as war-room curriculum
caseStudies.description: Broken Access Control, Cryptographic Failures, Injection, and Security Misconfiguration dominate real breach root causes.
caseStudies.analysis: Teaching beat: disclosure choices should name the failure class without inventing root cause before forensics finish.
caseStudies.outcomes: Teams that map incidents to OWASP classes brief boards faster and with less spin.

caseStudies.title: Capital One / Paige Thompson
caseStudies.description: Misconfigured WAF/S3 access led to ~100M records exposed; relatively fast public disclosure.
caseStudies.analysis: Fast facts + clear customer notice reduced narrative capture — still costly, but controllable.
caseStudies.outcomes: Criminal conviction of attacker; Capital One paid large fine but avoided Uber-style cover-up narrative.

caseStudies.title: LastPass multi-stage disclosure
caseStudies.description: Initial limited breach disclosure expanded as later stages (vault backups) became clear.
caseStudies.analysis: Partial truth early can be honest — or look like drip narrative capture if facts gap was avoidable.
caseStudies.outcomes: Customer migration; trust hit; example of staged disclosure under incomplete forensics.
